question: Among the absorbents compared with the [TEPAH][ATA] phase change absorbent, which has the highest CO2 loading, and at what temperature was it measured?
rendered:
<document title="Amino-Functionalized Ionic Liquid Phase Change Absorbents for Efficient CO2 Capture">

=== page 5 ===
- Similarly, the conventional AMP/MEA/H2O system, which has limited primary/secondary amine functionality, achieves only 0.5 mol mol^− 1.
- To evaluate the influence of desorption temperature and duration on regeneration efficiency, the CO2-saturated solution was subjected to thermal desorption under atmospheric pressure over a temperature range of 373.15−393.15 K. As depicted in Figure 6a, the regeneration efficiency increased with both rising temperature and extended time; at a fixed time point, a higher desorption temperature yielded greater regeneration efficiency.
- At 393.15 K and 80 min, the rich phase was regenerated efficiently, with a regeneration efficiency of 94.7%.
- Extending desorption time from 80 to 100 min at the same temperature did not improve regeneration efficiency.
- The rich phase was likely already fully desorbed within 80 min.
- Taking economic and energy consumption into account, the optimal regeneration conditions were established as a desorption temperature of 393.15 K and a duration of 80 min.
- As shown in Figure 6b, the regeneration efficiency remained at 88.6% of its initial value after five cycles, indicating that the absorbent maintains good stability after repeated regeneration.
- At 425.15 K, the sample retained 90% of its initial mass with no significant weight loss, which likely originated from residual moisture.
- Even at 500 K, the weight loss reached only 50%.
- In practical carbon capture processes, the absorption temperature typically ranges from 303.15 to 333.15 K, while desorption is conducted at 373.15−393.15 K.
